summary: The root زفف (zff) primarily describes a quick, light, or gliding motion, often with a rustling sound. It can refer to a bird's swift flight or the rustling of wings.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: زَفَّ العَرُوسَ, (K,) or زَفَفْتُهَا, (S,) or زَفَّتْهَا النِّسَآءُ, (Msb,) aor. زَفُفَ, (Msb, K,) inf. n. زَفٌّ (S, Msb, K) and زِفَافٌ, (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst.; (Msb;) and, (K,) or ازففتها, (S,) or ازفّتها النسآء; (Msb;) and, (K,) or ازدففتها, (S,) [or ازدفّتها النسآء;] إِلَى زَوْجِهَا; all signify the same; (S, Msb, * K;) i. e.

ازفّ, inf. n. إِزْفَافٌ, intrans.: see 1, in three places. ازفّ العَرُوسَ: see 1, first sentence. ازفّهُ He made him to hasten, or go quickly; (S, L, K;) namely, a camel, (S, L,) and an ostrich. (S.) [And accord. to Freytag, it occurs in the Deewán el-Hudhaleeyeen as meaning He led him to do light, vain, things. ]
ازدفّ العَرُوسَ: see 1, first sentence. ازدفّ الحِمْلَ He carried, took up and carried, or raised upon his back, the load. (Ibn-' Abbád, K.)

استزفّهُ السَّيْلُ, (Ibn-' Abbád, A, O, TA,) thus correctly, but in the copies of the K السَّيْرُ, (TA,) The torrent found it light to carry ( اِسْتَخَفَّهُ, Ibn-' Abbád, A, O, K), and took it away. (Ibn- ' Abbád, A, O, TA.)

R. Q. 1 زَفْزَفَ, [inf. n. زَفْزَفَةٌ,] said of a man, He walked in a comely manner. (TA.) زَفْزَفَةٌ also signifies The running vehemently. (K.) And A certain manner, or rate, of going, of camels, said to be beyond, or above, what is termed الخَبَبُ. (TA.) Said of a bird: see 1, latter part. And زَفْزَفَت said of the wind: see, again, 1, latter part. The inf. n.
R. Q. 1 تَزَفْرَفَتْ: see the next preceding paragraph, last sentence.

زِفٌّ Small feathers of the ostrich, (S, K,) and (S, in the K “ or ”) of a bird (S, K) of any kind: (K:) or small feathers, like down, beneath the thickset feathers: (IDrd, O, TA:) accord. to some, only of the ostrich: (O, TA:) [pl., app., زِفَافٌ: see زَفَازِفُ.] One says أَلْيَنُ مِنْ زِفِّ النَّعَامِ [ More soft than the small feathers of the ostrich ]. (TA.)

زَفَّةٌ (tropical:) A time; one time; syn. مَرَّةٌ: (K:) one says, جِئْتُهُ زَفَّةً, or زَفَّتَيْنِ, (tropical:) I came to him once, or twice. (TA.) A single act of زَفِيف [i. e. hastening, or going quickly ]. (TA. [This seems to be the primary signification.])

زُفَّةٌ A company, or congregated body, of men. (O, K.) Hence the saying of the Prophet to Bilál, on the occasion of the marriage of Fátimeh, أَدْخِلِ النَّاسَ عَلَىَّ زُفَّةً زُفَّةً, meaning Bring thou in the people to me company after company. (O, TA.)
زَفَفٌ, in a male ostrich, The quality of having abundant and dense زِفّ, i. e. small feathers. (S, K.)

زَفُوفٌ: see زَفْزَفٌ. Hence it is applied to a she-camel, as being likened to an ostrich in her quickness; (TA;) meaning [ Quick: or] good in pace, and quick. (Ham p. 750.) And الزَّفُوفُ is the name of a certain horse that belonged to Noamán Ibn-El-Mundhir. (O.) Also A twanging bow. (TA.)

زَفِيفٌ (S, K) and and, (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) or, without ى, (L, TA,) Quick, (Ibn-'Abbád, S, L, K,) like َفِيفٌ, (S,) and light. (L, TA. [In the CK the explanation is omitted.]) It is also an inf. n.: (S, K, &c.:) or a simple subst. (Msb.) [See 1, in several places.)
زِفَّانٌ: see the next preceding paragraph.
زِفَّانِىُّ: see the next preceding paragraph.

زَفْزَفٌ and [the latter of which is omitted in the CK] A wind that blows violently, with continuance; as also, (K, TA,) or زَفْزَفَةٌ: (CK:) or and زَفْزَفٌ a wind making a moaning ( حَنِين ), and sounding among the trees: (S:) or زَفْزَفٌ a quick, or swift, wind: or زَفْزَفَةٌ and and a violent wind, having a زَفْزَفَة, i. e. sounding: the pl. of زَفْزَفٌ is زَفَازِفُ. (TA.) Also, (i. e. the first and second words,) Light [ in motion or action ].
زَفْزَافٌ, and with ة: see the next preceding paragraph, in five places.

زَفَازِفُ pl. of زَفْزَفٌ. It is also used by a Hudhalee poet [app. referring to birds] as meaning َوَاتُ زِفَافٍ [i. e., supposing زِفَاف to be pl. of زِفٌّ, agreeably with analogy, Having small, downy, feathers ]. (TA.)

[ زَافٌّ act. part. n. of زَفَّ in the phrase زَفَّ العَرُوسَ: fem. with ة: pl. of the latter زَوَافُّ. Hence,] زَحَفَتْ زَوَافُّهَا, a phrase mentioned by Lh, meaning اللَّوَاتِىزَفَفْنَهَا [i. e. The women who conducted her to her husband walked along gently ]. (TA.)
أَزَفُّ A male ostrich having abundant and dense زِفّ, i. e. small feathers. (S, K.) See also زَفِيفٌ.
مِزَفَّةٌ A [ vehicle of the kind called ] مِحَفَّةٌ in which, or upon which, the bride is sent [or conducted ] to her husband. (Kh, S, K.)

[ مَزْفُوفٌ pass. part. n. of زَفَّ in a sense not mentioned, and perhaps not used. Hence,] بَاتَ مَزْفُوفًا a phrase meaning بات تُزَفْزِفُهُ الرِّيحُ [i. e. He passed the night made to tremble, or quake, by the wind ]. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
